<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/system/ -->

# System

Identity, saving, resetting, errors, the watchdog, the heartbeat and the settings.

### Send_CAN_ID

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 11</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">1 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_CAN_ID()`</span></div>

Gives the driver a new node ID, 0 to 13 (the firmware accepts up to 15, but the bootloader reserves 14 and 15: a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN). Saving the configuration (Send_Save_config) also writes the ID into the bootloader's board ID. The driver answers to the new ID at once; the ID is kept over a power cycle only after Send_Save_config.

**1 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | ID | unsigned 8-bit | 0 to 13; 14 and 15 are accepted but reserved by the bootloader |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_ESTOP

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 0</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_ESTOP()`</span></div>

Stops the motor and raises the E-stop error, which stays until Send_Clear_Error.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Idle

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 12</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Idle()`</span></div>

Puts the driver in idle mode (the motor coasts or brakes, see Send_Settings).

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Save_config

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 13</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Save_config()`</span></div>

Writes the current configuration (gains, limits, calibration, CAN ID, heartbeat, watchdog, gripper flag) to the EEPROM, and the CAN ID into the bootloader's board ID. From firmware 109 it also writes the tool id and the watchdog fallback (settings block 2), the anti-cogging set with its mode and scale, and the encoder table with its on/off flag, parameter 56 and the current-sense zero trims, each block with its own checksum; of the two large blocks only the 16-byte pages that changed are written. Not kept: the idle behaviour of Send_Settings, the current loop bandwidth, and every parameter the parameter table marks as not kept. It also writes the serial number held in RAM, which is 1 after a power-up unless `#SERNUM` set it, over the stored one. A drive stopped by the product lock writes nothing.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Reset

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 14</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Reset()`</span></div>

Resets the driver. From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again; this is how a firmware update begins.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Clear_Error

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 1</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Clear_Error()`</span></div>

Clears the error flags and goes to idle; it also ends a watchdog hold or descend. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back. A calibration error is cleared only by calibrating. A gripper E-stop comes back until the E-stop bit of Send_gripper_data_pack is 0 again.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Watchdog

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 15</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Watchdog()`</span></div>

Sets the watchdog: when the time runs out the driver reports a watchdog error and does what the action byte says. Every valid motion frame (Send_data_pack_1, Send_data_pack_PD, Send_data_pack_HALL, Send_gripper_data_pack) and every request the driver answers (status requests, Send_Get_Parameter, Send_Buffer_Read) resets it. From firmware 109 so do Send_Save_config and Send_Watchdog itself, which starts a fresh window. The other setting frames (gains, limits, Idle, Clear, Settings, Send_Parameter) do not. 0 turns it off (the default). From firmware 109 the driver acts on the action byte, but only when the watchdog is the only active error: any other error gets the legacy response. Hold and descend run for the fallback time (parameter 2, 2 s by default), then the after-action (parameter 5); they start only if the driver was in position, velocity, current, PD or gripper mode, otherwise it stays as idle was. [The watchdog](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/06-operation/watchdog/) explains each action. Send_Save_config keeps the watchdog, and a kept watchdog runs from power-up: a host that sends nothing within the time finds the driver in watchdog error, and clears it with Send_Clear_Error. The same values are parameters 6 and 7.

**5 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Time | unsigned 32-bit | ms; 0 = off |
| 4 |  | Action | unsigned 8-bit | 0 legacy (brake or coast as idle does), 1 hold the position, 2 brake, 3 coast, 4 descend at the fallback current and speed; other values act as 0 |

The driver does not answer this command.

Firmware 108 and older store the action byte without acting on it. The Python library sends all five actions from 1.21 ('Idle', 'Hold', 'Brake', 'Coast', 'Descend'); 1.20 and older send only 0, 1 or 2.

---

### Send_Heartbeat_Setup

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 30</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Heartbeat_Setup()`</span></div>

Sets the heartbeat interval in ms; 0 turns the heartbeat off (the default). Kept by Send_Save_config.

**4 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Interval | unsigned 32-bit | ms; 0 = off |

---

### Send_Settings

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 35</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">2 to 8 bytes</span></div>

Sets boolean settings that have no command of their own: a mask byte says which settings the frame touches, a value byte gives their new values; settings outside the mask are left alone. Bit 0 is the idle behaviour: 1 brake (phases shorted), 0 coast. The setting is not kept by Send_Save_config: at power-up the driver brakes. Added in firmware 107. The Python library has Send_Settings and Send_Brake_Coast from 1.21; 1.20 and older have no call for it.

**2 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Mask | unsigned 8-bit | bit 0 = write the idle behaviour |
| 1 |  | Value | unsigned 8-bit | bit 0: 1 brake, 0 coast |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Cyclic_command

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 29</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">not implemented</span></div>

Reserved. The firmware has no handler for this ID and the Python library's call does nothing.

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/parameters/ -->

# Parameters and buffers

From firmware 109 a setting that has no command of its own is a **parameter**: a number from 1 to 87 behind one
pair of commands, Send_Parameter (ID 36) to set it and Send_Get_Parameter (ID 37) to read it, answered with
Respond_Parameter (ID 38). The identifier has room for only 64 command IDs, so new settings no longer use them up.
Parameter numbers are permanent: a number is never given a new meaning. Number 73 is not used and stays free.

The **buffers** are the larger data a drive holds: a capture of three signals, a histogram, the anti-cogging set
and the encoder table. Send_Buffer_Read (ID 41) reads them in 8-byte frames, Respond_Buffer_Data (ID 42) carries
them, and Send_Buffer_Write (ID 43) writes the anti-cogging set.

Over UART, `#Par` does the same: `#Par` lists every parameter, `#Par 56` reads one, `#Par 56,0` sets it
([Status and utility](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/uart/utility/)).

## Setting and reading a parameter

A set is not answered: read the value back to know what the driver took. A value outside a parameter's range is
clamped, replaced or refused, as the table says, and a read-only number ignores the write.

```python
import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral

comms = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM41', bitrate=1000000)
motor = Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=0, communication=comms)

motor.Send_Parameter(56, 0)                # nothing runs by itself after the next #Calangle
motor.Send_Get_Parameter(56)               # read it back
message, ids = comms.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.1)
if message is not None:
    motor.UnpackData(message, ids)
print(motor.parameters.get(56))
motor.Send_Save_config()                   # keep it over a power cycle
```

`Send_Parameter`, `Send_Get_Parameter` and the buffer calls need the Spectral-BLDC library 1.21 or newer.
`Send_Parameter` takes the value itself: a gain or a limit (8 to 16 and 20) is sent as a float, so
`motor.Send_Parameter(16, 1500)` sets a current limit of 1500 mA; every other parameter takes a whole number.

## The commands

### Send_Parameter

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 36</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Parameter()`</span></div>

Sets one parameter by its number (the [parameter table](#every-parameter)). Firmware 109 gives new settings a parameter number instead of a command ID of their own, since the identifier has room for only 64 command IDs. A value outside a parameter's range is clamped, replaced or refused as the table says; a number the firmware does not know, or a read-only one, is ignored. The driver does not answer: read the value back with Send_Get_Parameter. A value set this way lives in RAM until Send_Save_config, like every other setting; the table says which parameters Save keeps.

**5 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Parameter | unsigned 8-bit | the parameter number, 1-87 |
| 1-4 |  | Value | signed 32-bit | the new value, in the parameter's unit; for the gains, limits and Kt (8-16, 20) a float's bit pattern |

The driver does not answer this command.

A data frame of another length, or a remote frame, is ignored and flagged as a wrong data length. It does not reset the watchdog.

---

### Send_Get_Parameter

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 37</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">1 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Get_Parameter()`</span></div>

Asks for the value in force of one parameter. The answer, Respond_Parameter, comes under ID 38, not 37: a host and a driver must never send data frames with the same identifier, because two sent at the same moment collide. Resets the watchdog. The Python library stores the value in `parameters[number]`.

**1 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Parameter | unsigned 8-bit | the parameter number |

The driver answers with **Respond_Parameter**.

---

### Respond_Parameter

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 38</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">5 bytes</span></div>

The answer to Send_Get_Parameter: the number and the value in force. For a number the firmware does not know the frame carries the number alone (1 byte; the Python library sets `unknown_parameter`). The gains, limits and Kt (parameters 8 to 16 and 20) travel as the bit pattern of an IEEE-754 float, the others as integers.

**The frame** (5 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | parameter | unsigned 8-bit | the parameter number |
| 1-4 |  | value | signed 32-bit | the value in force; a float's bits for 8-16 and 20 |

---

### Send_Buffer_Read

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 41</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Buffer_Read()`</span></div>

Asks for entries of one of the drive's buffers: the capture, the histogram, the anti-cogging harmonics or table, or the encoder table. The driver answers with one Respond_Buffer_Data frame per entry (for the two tables, one per three values), sent from its main loop whenever a transmit mailbox is free, so a long read-out never holds up the control loop or other answers. A new request replaces one still in progress; count 0 cancels it. Entries past the end are not sent. Resets the watchdog.

**5 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Kind | unsigned 8-bit | 0 capture (up to 1024 samples: parameter 32 says how many), 1 histogram (256 bins), 2 anti-cogging harmonics (8 slots), 3 anti-cogging table (256 values), 4 encoder table (128 values) |
| 1-2 |  | First | unsigned 16-bit | the first index |
| 3-4 |  | Count | unsigned 16-bit | how many entries; 0 cancels a read-out |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Respond_Buffer_Data

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 42</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span></div>

One entry of a buffer, the answer to Send_Buffer_Read. The first two bytes say which: the kind in the top three bits, the index in the other thirteen (kind × 8192 + index). The six bytes after them depend on the kind, as the table below the frame says.

**The frame** (8 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 |  | header | unsigned 16-bit | kind × 8192 + index |
| 2-3 |  | word_a | signed 16-bit | capture: channel A; histogram: the count (unsigned); harmonics: the harmonic number (0 = slot unused); tables: entry index |
| 4-5 |  | word_b | signed 16-bit | capture: channel B; histogram: the sum's upper 16 bits; harmonics: a, the cosine term in mA; tables: entry index + 1 |
| 6-7 |  | word_c | signed 16-bit | capture: channel C; histogram: the sum's lower 16 bits; harmonics: b, the sine term in mA; tables: entry index + 2 (0 past the end) |

| Kind | Index | Bytes 2-7 |
|---|---|---|
| 0 capture | the sample, oldest first, 0 to parameter 32 − 1 | channels A, B and C, each in its signal's unit (the parameter table lists the signals) |
| 1 histogram | the bin, 0-255 over one electrical turn or one motor turn | the count (unsigned 16-bit), then the sum (signed 32-bit); the bin's mean is sum ÷ count |
| 2 anti-cogging harmonics | the slot, 0-7 | the harmonic of the electrical angle (1-32, 0 = unused), a and b in mA: the slot adds a·cos(h·θ) + b·sin(h·θ) |
| 3 anti-cogging table | the first of three values, 0-255 | three values in mA, 64 angle counts apart (256 per electrical turn) |
| 4 encoder table | the first of three values, 0-127 | three corrections in 1/16 encoder count, 128 per motor turn |

---

### Send_Buffer_Write

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 43</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Cogging_Harmonic(), Send_Cogging_Table()`</span></div>

Writes the anti-cogging set: kind 2 one harmonic slot per frame, kind 3 three table values per frame, in the Respond_Buffer_Data layout. Other kinds are ignored (the encoder table cannot be written), and so is a harmonic above 32. The set lives in RAM until Send_Save_config; switch it on with parameter 37. The driver does not answer.

**8 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 |  | Header | unsigned 16-bit | kind × 8192 + index; kind 2 or 3 |
| 2-3 |  | Word A | signed 16-bit | kind 2: the harmonic (1-32, 0 = unused); kind 3: value at index |
| 4-5 |  | Word B | signed 16-bit | kind 2: a in mA; kind 3: value at index + 1 |
| 6-7 |  | Word C | signed 16-bit | kind 2: b in mA; kind 3: value at index + 2 |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

## Every parameter

The number and the name are read from the firmware; the rest is checked against its source. *Access*: a read-only
parameter ignores a write; a run parameter starts or stops a run when written and gives its state when read.

### Watchdog and tool

Parameters 1 to 5 live in settings block 2 of the EEPROM, 6 and 7 in the first settings block beside the other settings; Send_Save_config keeps all seven. A value outside a range is clamped, replaced or ignored, as the Value column says.

| No. | Name | Access | Value | Kept by Save | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `PARAM_TOOL_ID` | set, read | 0 none, 1 SSG-48, 11-33 MSG, 200-254 your own tools; a value outside 0-255 is ignored. Default 0 | yes, settings block 2 | What the drive is built into. For an MSG the tens digit is the rail (1 = 100, 2 = 150, 3 = 200 mm) and the units digit the stepper (1 = 21.5, 2 = 40, 3 = 60 mm). Also `#Tool`; reported in the identity frame. |
| 2 | `PARAM_WD_FALLBACK_TIME` | set, read | ms, 0-60000 (clamped). Default 2000 | yes, settings block 2 | How long watchdog hold or descend runs before the after-action takes over. |
| 3 | `PARAM_WD_FALLBACK_CURRENT` | set, read | mA, signed, -32768 to 32767 (outside: 0). Default 0 | yes, settings block 2 | The current watchdog descend applies. 0 lets gravity lower a joint; a gripper gets its grip current. |
| 4 | `PARAM_WD_FALLBACK_SPEED` | set, read | ticks/s, 0-65535 (outside: 1000). Default 1000 | yes, settings block 2 | The speed watchdog descend never exceeds, in either direction. |
| 5 | `PARAM_WD_AFTER_ACTION` | set, read | 0 legacy, 2 brake, 3 coast (any other value: 0). Default 0 | yes, settings block 2 | What follows hold or descend when the fallback time has run out. |
| 6 | `PARAM_WD_TIME` | set, read | ms, 0 = off (a negative value: 0). Default 0 | yes, settings block 1 | The watchdog time, the same value Send_Watchdog sets. |
| 7 | `PARAM_WD_ACTION` | set, read | 0 legacy, 1 hold, 2 brake, 3 coast, 4 descend (outside 0-255: 0; 5-255 act as legacy). Default 0 | yes, settings block 1 | What a trip of the watchdog alone does, the same value as byte 4 of Send_Watchdog. |

### Gains, limits and settings

The values in force, readable and writable by parameter (their own commands, given in each row, still work). A float travels as its IEEE-754 bit pattern, big-endian, the way the gain commands send it; over UART `#Par 9,0.02` sets Kpv. A write goes to RAM like the commands' own; Send_Save_config keeps it. Parameter 23, the product stamp, stays read only.

| No. | Name | Access | Value | Kept by Save | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | `PARAM_KPP` | set, read | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) | yes | Kp of the position loop (Send_Position_Gains, `#Kpp`). |
| 9 | `PARAM_KPV` | set, read | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) | yes | Kp of the velocity loop (Send_Velocity_Gains, `#Kpv`). |
| 10 | `PARAM_KIV` | set, read | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) | yes | Ki of the velocity loop (Send_Velocity_Gains, `#Kiv`). |
| 11 | `PARAM_KPIQ` | set, read | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) | yes | Kp of the current loops; writing it sets the Iq and the Id loop, as `#Kpiq` does (Send_Current_Gains sets the Iq loop only). A calibration and parameter 49 set it too. |
| 12 | `PARAM_KIIQ` | set, read | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) | yes | Ki of the current loops; writing it sets the Iq and the Id loop, as `#Kiiq` does (Send_Current_Gains sets the Iq loop only). A calibration and parameter 49 set it too. |
| 13 | `PARAM_KP` | set, read | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) | yes | KP, the stiffness of the impedance (PD) loop (Send_PD_Gains). |
| 14 | `PARAM_KD` | set, read | float; 0 or more, below 10^9 (negative or not a number: refused) | yes | KD, the damping of the impedance (PD) loop (Send_PD_Gains). |
| 15 | `PARAM_VELOCITY_LIMIT` | set, read | float, ticks/s; 0 or more, below 10^9 (otherwise refused) | yes | The velocity limit (Send_Limits, `#Vlimit`). |
| 16 | `PARAM_CURRENT_LIMIT` | set, read | float, mA; 0-2800 (negative or above 2800: refused) | yes | The current limit (Send_Limits, `#Ilim`). |
| 17 | `PARAM_VOLTAGE_LIMIT` | set, read | mV, 0-60000 (outside: refused); 0 = the supply voltage | yes | The voltage limit of the current loops (Send_Voltage_Limit, `#Vlim`). |
| 18 | `PARAM_BRAKE_COAST` | set, read | 1 brake, 0 coast (any value but 0: brake) | no: the driver brakes at every power-up | The idle behaviour (Send_Settings bit 0, `#Brake`, `#Coast`). |
| 19 | `PARAM_HEARTBEAT_MS` | set, read | ms, 0-60000 (outside: refused); 0 = off | yes | The heartbeat interval (Send_Heartbeat_Setup). |
| 20 | `PARAM_KT` | set, read | float, Nm/A; 0 or more, below 10^9 (otherwise refused) | yes | The torque constant (Send_Kt, `#Kt`, calibration). |
| 23 | `PARAM_BOARD_PRODUCT` | read only | 1 STEPFOC, 2 Spectral Micro, 0 none | yes, settings block 2 (stamped by the firmware) | The product lock: the product that calibrated this board. Stamped at the first start-up of a calibrated board and at every save. A firmware that finds the other product's stamp drives nothing (see Errors). |

### The motor

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 76 | `PARAM_R_MOHM` | set, read | mΩ, 1-100000 (outside: refused) | yes, with the calibration | The phase resistance of one coil, the same value as `#R` (in Ω there). The current gains follow at the next calibration or when parameter 49 is written. |
| 77 | `PARAM_L_UH` | set, read | µH, 1-1000000 (outside: refused) | yes, with the calibration | The phase inductance of one coil, the same value as `#L` (in H there). The current gains follow at the next calibration or when parameter 49 is written. |

### Current sensing and the current loop

The current-sense zero is the ADC reading with no current flowing, in counts from 2048 (1 count is about 1.6 mA). The driver measures it at every start-up with the bridge off; the trim is added to it.

| No. | Name | Access | Value | Kept by Save | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 21 | `PARAM_SENSE1_OFFSET` | set, read | counts from 2048, -400 to 400 (outside: refused) | no: measured again at every start-up | The current-sense zero of channel 1 in use. Measured at start-up (the trim, 59, added); writable for tests, until the next start-up. |
| 22 | `PARAM_SENSE2_OFFSET` | set, read | counts from 2048, -400 to 400 (outside: refused) | no: measured again at every start-up | The current-sense zero of channel 2 in use, as 21. |
| 40 | `PARAM_SENSE1_OFFSET_OFF` | read only | counts from 2048 | no: measured at every start-up | The zero of channel 1 measured with the bridge off, the trim added. |
| 41 | `PARAM_SENSE2_OFFSET_OFF` | read only | counts from 2048 | no: measured at every start-up | The zero of channel 2 measured with the bridge off, the trim added. |
| 42 | `PARAM_SENSE_ZERO_SWITCHING` | read only | 0 not run, 1 measuring, 2 in use, 3 rejected (implausible), 4 interrupted (a command or an error came first), 5 measured, not in use | no | The second zero measurement, made in idle after start-up with the bridge switching at 50 % duty. On the bench it made the current ripple worse, so it is measured and kept but not used unless 46 asks for it. |
| 46 | `PARAM_SENSE_ZERO_USE_SWITCHING` | set, read | 1 the zero measured with the bridge switching, 0 the bridge-off zero. Default 0 | no | Which zero is in use. 1 takes effect only while 42 reads 5 (measured, not in use). |
| 47 | `PARAM_SENSE1_OFFSET_SW` | read only | counts from 2048 | no | The zero of channel 1 measured with the bridge switching. |
| 48 | `PARAM_SENSE2_OFFSET_SW` | read only | counts from 2048 | no | The zero of channel 2 measured with the bridge switching. |
| 49 | `PARAM_CURRENT_BANDWIDTH` | set, read | Hz, 10-625 (outside, or with R or L not set: refused). 160 at every start-up | no; the gains it sets are kept by Save | Writing it sets Kp_iq and Ki_iq at once from R, L and this bandwidth, as `#Cbw` does. Reading gives the bandwidth the gains in force amount to with the R and L in force (0 without them). |
| 58 | `PARAM_ID_SETPOINT` | set, read | mA, -3000 to 3000 (outside: refused). Default 0 | no | The d-axis current setpoint, as `#Id`. It makes no torque, only more current in the coils. |
| 59 | `PARAM_ZERO_TRIM1` | set, read | counts, -60 to 60 (outside: refused). Default 0 | yes, encoder block | The trim added to the zero of channel 1 measured at every start-up. The anti-cogging identification with the trim (43 = 4 or 5, and the runs after a calibration) sets it; writing it moves the zero in use at once. |
| 60 | `PARAM_ZERO_TRIM2` | set, read | counts, -60 to 60 (outside: refused). Default 0 | yes, encoder block | The trim of channel 2, as 59. |
| 61 | `PARAM_THETA_OFFSET` | read only | 0.1° electrical | yes, with the calibration | The electrical offset between the encoder and the motor, found by calibration (`#Offset` in rad). |
| 62 | `PARAM_TRIM_H1_BEFORE` | read only | 0.1 mA | no | The 1st harmonic of the anti-cogging set before the last trim, the error the trim corrects. |
| 63 | `PARAM_TRIM_H1_AFTER` | read only | 0.1 mA | no | The 1st harmonic after the last trim. A trim that does not lower it by 30 % is taken back. |
| 64 | `PARAM_COMM_DELAY_US` | set, read | µs, 0-500 (outside: refused), 0 = off. Default 166 | no: 166 at every start-up | Commutation delay compensation: the output voltage is turned forward by the angle the rotor covers in this time. Applied in the closed-loop modes above 100 ticks/s. |
| 65 | `PARAM_FAST_TRIG` | set, read | 1 from the integer sine table, 0 from the float routine. Default 0 | no | Where the transforms of every control loop take sin and cos from. The table was not faster on the bench. |

### Capture and histogram

The signal numbers: 0 none, 1 measured Iq (mA), 2 measured Id (mA), 3 Iq setpoint with the anti-cogging (mA), 4 speed (ticks/s, saturates at ±32767), 5 speed ÷ 16, 6 position (ticks, the low 16 bits), 7 position error (ticks), 8 electrical angle (0-16383 per electrical turn, from the encoder alone), 9 encoder (0-16383 per motor turn), 10 Vbus (10 mV), 11 and 12 the two current-sense readings (counts after the zero), 13 the control interrupt's time (µs), 14 the anti-cogging feedforward (mA), 15 the Iq setpoint without the anti-cogging (mA), 16 the Uq setpoint (mV), 17 and 18 the d and q voltage the output transform received (mV). None of these settings is saved.

| No. | Name | Access | Value | Kept by Save | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24 | `PARAM_CAPTURE_SOURCE_A` | set, read | signal 0-18 (outside: 0). Default 4, speed | no | The signal of channel A, which is also the trigger channel. |
| 25 | `PARAM_CAPTURE_SOURCE_B` | set, read | signal 0-18 (outside: 0). Default 1, Iq | no | The signal of channel B. |
| 26 | `PARAM_CAPTURE_SOURCE_C` | set, read | signal 0-18 (outside: 0). Default 8, electrical angle | no | The signal of channel C. |
| 27 | `PARAM_CAPTURE_DIVIDER` | set, read | control loops per sample, 1-65535 (clamped). Default 1 | no | One sample every N control loops of 160 µs. |
| 28 | `PARAM_CAPTURE_TRIGGER` | set, read | 0 stop, 1 now, 2 on an error, 3 channel A rising through the level, 4 falling through it (outside: 0) | no | 1 to 4 clear the buffer and arm a capture; 0 stops one and keeps what was recorded. The error trigger fires when the error flag rises, a watchdog trip included; an error already present does not fire it. |
| 29 | `PARAM_CAPTURE_LEVEL` | set, read | channel A's unit, -32768 to 32767 (saturated). Default 0 | no | The level of triggers 3 and 4. |
| 30 | `PARAM_CAPTURE_PRETRIGGER` | set, read | samples, 0-1023 (clamped). Default 0 | no | How many samples from before the trigger the capture keeps. |
| 31 | `PARAM_CAPTURE_STATE` | read only | 0 idle, 1 armed, 2 recording, 3 done | no | Where the capture stands. |
| 32 | `PARAM_CAPTURE_COUNT` | read only | samples, 0-1024 | no | The samples readable with buffer kind 0. |
| 33 | `PARAM_CAPTURE_TRIGGER_INDEX` | read only | sample index; -1 before a trigger | no | Which sample of the read-out is the trigger sample. |
| 34 | `PARAM_HIST_X` | set, read | 0 off, 1 electrical angle, 2 encoder (256 bins each; outside: 0) | no | 1 or 2 clear the histogram and start it; 0 stops it and keeps the data readable. |
| 35 | `PARAM_HIST_Y` | set, read | signal 0-18 (outside: 0). Default 3, Iq setpoint | no | The signal summed per bin. Set it before 34. |
| 36 | `PARAM_HIST_SAMPLES` | read only | samples | no | Samples summed since the start. The histogram stops by itself when one bin holds 65535. |
| 39 | `PARAM_CAPTURE_LENGTH` | read only | 1024 | — | The samples per channel a capture holds. |

### Sound

None of the sound settings is saved; see [Sound](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/06-operation/sound/).

| No. | Name | Access | Value | Kept by Save | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 80 | `PARAM_SOUND_STATE` | read only | bits 0-7 events queued, 8-18 samples buffered, 24 a tone sounds, 25 the queue plays, 26 samples play, 27 the samples ran dry | — | What the sound is doing; a host that refills the queue or the sample buffer reads it. |
| 81 | `PARAM_SOUND_LIMIT_MV` | set, read | mV, 0-6000 (outside: refused). Default 2000; 0 refuses sound and stops what plays | no: 2000 at every start-up | The sound's voltage at most, all tones and samples together. |
| 82 | `PARAM_SOUND_AXIS` | set, read | 1 the q axis (default), 0 the d axis (outside: refused) | no: 1 at every start-up | Which axis carries the sound. The q axis makes torque, a small ripple at the tone's pitch, and was much louder on the bench; the d axis makes no torque and is quieter. |

### Status

| No. | Name | Access | Value | Kept by Save | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 79 | `PARAM_FEATURES` | read only | bits, see What is in force | — | What is in force and what is running, one bit each. |
| 83 | `PARAM_STACK_UNUSED` | read only | bytes; -1 if it was not measured | — | The stack margin: RAM between the heap and the stack that the stack has not used since start-up (setup() fills it with a pattern at its end, and this counts the bytes the pattern is still in). The stack needs about 1.5 to 2 KB of the about 7 KB there are; a value far below that means the drive is short of RAM. |
| 84 | `PARAM_BUILD_COMMIT` | read only | the commit's first 7 hex digits as a number (bits 0-27); bit 28 set: built with uncommitted changes; 0 when git was not available at the build | — | The git commit the firmware was built from. `#Info` prints it as `Build:`, with a `+` for bit 28. |
| 85 | `PARAM_BUILD_TIME` | read only | Unix seconds, UTC; 0 when the build did not set it | — | When the firmware was built. |
| 86 | `PARAM_BOARD_ID` | read only | 32 bits, read as unsigned | — | This board: the chip's factory-unique 96-bit number folded into 32 bits. It never changes, also not with a new firmware or `#Default`. `#Info` prints it as `Board ID:`, 8 hex digits. |
| 87 | `PARAM_CALIBRATION_ID` | read only | 32 bits, read as unsigned; 0 before the first calibration | yes, settings block 2 | A new number at every successful `#Cal`, `#Calonly` or `#Calangle`, so a host can tell one calibration from the next. Send_Save_config keeps it, and `#Default` sets it back to 0. `#Info` prints it as `Calibration ID:`, 8 hex digits. |

## What is in force: parameter 79

Parameter 79 says in one read what the drive runs with. `#Info` prints the same at its end, under `In force:`.
Bit 0 is the least significant.

| Bit | Set when |
|---|---|
| 0 | the motor is calibrated |
| 1 | an encoder table is measured (in RAM) |
| 2 | the encoder table is in use (parameter 53) |
| 3 | an anti-cogging set is in RAM (harmonics or table) |
| 4 | anti-cogging is on (parameter 37 not 0) |
| 5 | anti-cogging is on as the table (otherwise as the harmonics) |
| 6 | the anti-cogging set in RAM is the one saved in the EEPROM |
| 7 | a current-sense zero trim is applied (parameter 59 or 60 not 0) |
| 8 | the current-sense zero measured with the bridge switching is in use (parameter 46) |
| 9 | commutation delay compensation is on (parameter 64 not 0) |
| 10 | the speed estimate is a PLL (parameter 50 is 1 or 2) |
| 11 | fast reading is on (parameter 71) |
| 12 | fast PWM is on (parameter 72) |
| 13 | sin and cos come from the integer table (parameter 65) |
| 14 | the position input filter is on (parameter 74 not 0) |
| 15 | the velocity-integral deadband is on (parameter 75 not 0) |
| 16-17 | parameter 56: what follows a `#Calangle`, 0 nothing, 1 or 2 the anti-cogging |
| 20 | a calibration is running (also `#Calangle`'s search) |
| 21 | the encoder table is being measured |
| 22 | the anti-cogging is being identified |
| 23 | the runs after a calibration are about to start |
| 24 | sound is playing ([Sound](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/06-operation/sound/)) |

Bits 18, 19 and 25 to 31 are 0.

## Reading the capture

A capture records three signals inside the control loop, one sample every *divider* loops, 1024 samples per
channel. It starts when parameter 28 is written: at once (1), when the error flag rises (2, a watchdog trip
included), or when channel A rises (3) or falls (4) through the level of parameter 29. Parameter 30 keeps that many
samples from before the trigger. [Status and diagnostics](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/06-operation/diagnostics/) shows a whole capture.

1. Set the signals (24, 25, 26), the divider (27), the pre-trigger (30) and, for 3 and 4, the level (29).
2. Write the trigger (28). Parameter 31 reads 1 (armed), 2 (recording), then 3 (done).
3. Read parameter 32 (samples readable) and 33 (the trigger sample's index, −1 if none).
4. Send_Buffer_Read with kind 0, first 0, count = parameter 32: one Respond_Buffer_Data frame per sample, oldest
   first.

The histogram works the same way with parameters 34 to 36 and kind 1: it adds a signal into 256 bins by the
electrical angle or by the encoder, every control loop, until it is stopped or one bin holds 65535 samples.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/sound/ -->

# Sound

Sound through the motor: tones, a queue of timed events and samples, added to the output voltage while the
driver holds or moves. [Sound](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/06-operation/sound/) explains how to use them; parameters 80 to 82 are in the
[parameter table](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/parameters/#sound).

### Send_Sound

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 44</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Sound()`</span></div>

Plays sound through the motor: a tone now, a queue of timed events, or samples. The sound is added to the output voltage, on the q axis by default (parameter 82), and only while the driver holds or moves (position, velocity, current or PD mode); idle or an error stops all of it. Up to 4 tones sound at once (channels 0 to 3), from 20 Hz to below 3125 Hz, half the control-loop rate. Loudness is given as a current: the driver turns it into a voltage with the coil's impedance at that pitch, so low and high notes sound alike. The total voltage is limited to parameter 81 (2000 mV by default; 0 refuses sound). Added in firmware 109. The driver does not answer; parameter 80 says what plays. The Python library wraps the operations as Send_Tone, Send_Sound_Stop, Send_Sound_Event, Send_Sound_Play, Send_Sound_Clear, Send_Samples_Play and Send_Samples_Stop.

**8 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Operation | unsigned 8-bit | 0 stop everything (tones, queue, samples); 1 a tone now; 2 add an event to the queue; 3 play the queue; 4 play the samples; 5 samples off, buffer cleared; 6 clear the queue (tones that sound keep sounding) |
| 1 |  | Channel | unsigned 8-bit | the tone channel, 0-3 (operations 1 and 2) |
| 2-3 |  | A | unsigned 16-bit | 1, 2: the pitch in Hz (2: 0 silences the channel); 4: the sample rate in Hz, at most the loop rate |
| 4-5 |  | B | unsigned 16-bit | 1, 2: the loudness in mA; 4: the voltage of a full-scale sample in mV |
| 6-7 |  | C | unsigned 16-bit | 1: the duration in ms, 0 = until stopped; 2: the wait in ms before the next event, 0 = the next one starts with it |

The driver does not answer this command.

The queue holds 31 events and is played by the control loop with loop-exact timing: an event sets one channel's pitch and loudness, then waits. A chord is three events with wait 0 and a fourth with the chord's length. When the queue runs out, every channel falls silent. An event sent to a full queue is dropped. Samples: send them first with Send_Sound_Samples, then operation 4; the driver plays them at the given rate and stops when the buffer runs dry. A frame of another length, or a remote frame, is ignored. It does not reset the watchdog.

---

### Send_Sound_Samples

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 45</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">1 to 8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Samples()`</span></div>

Appends 1 to 8 samples (signed 8-bit, one per byte, −127 to 127 = full scale) to the driver's 1024-place sample buffer, which holds 1023 samples. Samples that do not fit are dropped; parameter 80 says how many are buffered. Send_Sound with operation 4 plays them. Added in firmware 109. The driver does not answer.

**8 bytes** — eight samples; a shorter frame carries fewer

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Sample 1 | signed 8-bit | the next sample |
| 1 |  | Sample 2 | signed 8-bit |  |
| 2 |  | Sample 3 | signed 8-bit |  |
| 3 |  | Sample 4 | signed 8-bit |  |
| 4 |  | Sample 5 | signed 8-bit |  |
| 5 |  | Sample 6 | signed 8-bit |  |
| 6 |  | Sample 7 | signed 8-bit |  |
| 7 |  | Sample 8 | signed 8-bit |  |

The driver does not answer this command.

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/gripper/ -->

# Gripper

The commands of gripper mode (`#Gripper 1`, saved).

### Send_gripper_data_pack

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 61</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 or 5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_gripper_data_pack()`</span></div>

The gripper command, for a driver set up as a gripper (`#Gripper 1`, saved). Position, speed and the current limit of the move, plus the activate, action and E-stop bits. A move is carried out only while the gripper is calibrated, activated and the action bit is 1. An empty frame (0 bytes) only asks for the state.

**5 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Position | unsigned 8-bit | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed |
| 1 |  | Speed | unsigned 8-bit | 0 slowest, 255 fastest |
| 2-3 |  | Current | signed 16-bit | current limit of the move in mA; from firmware 109 the move uses its magnitude, at most the driver's 2800 mA; see the gripper manual for the safe range |
| 4 | 7 | Activate | bit | 1 activate the gripper, 0 deactivate |
| 4 | 6 | Action | bit | 1 go to the position, 0 idle |
| 4 | 5 | E-stop | bit | 1 raises the gripper E-stop error, again on every control cycle until a frame with this bit 0 arrives; then Send_Clear_Error |
| 4 | 4 | Release direction | bit | read by the firmware but not used |

The driver answers with **Respond_Gripper_data_pack**.

---

### Send_gripper_calibrate

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 62</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_gripper_calibrate()`</span></div>

Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Needed after every power-up.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Respond_Gripper_data_pack

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 60</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span></div>

The driver's answer to Send_gripper_data_pack: position, measured current, and the state bits. Python attributes `gripper_position`, `gripper_current`, `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`, `gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error`, `gripper_calibrated`. The Python library 1.20 and older combine the two object-detection bits the wrong way round, so their `gripper_object_detection` reads 2 for an object found while closing and 1 for one found while opening; 1.21 and newer read them as the table says.

**The frame** (4 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | gripper_position | unsigned 8-bit | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed |
| 1-2 |  | gripper_current | signed 16-bit | measured current in mA |
| 3 | 7 | gripper_activated | bit | 1 activated |
| 3 | 6 | gripper_action_status | bit | the action bit of the last Send_gripper_data_pack (1 after #Grippos); the driver never clears it, so it stays 1 after the move ends: the object detection tells when the move has ended |
| 3 | 5-4 | gripper_object_detection | 2 bits | bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit: 0 moving, 1 object detected while closing, 2 object detected while opening, 3 at the position |
| 3 | 3 | gripper_temperature_error | bit | a copy of the thermistor temperature error |
| 3 | 2 | gripper_timeout_error | bit | a copy of the CAN watchdog error (Send_Watchdog), not a move timeout |
| 3 | 1 | gripper_estop_error | bit | the E-stop bit of Send_gripper_data_pack (or #Gripstop 1) was set |
| 3 | 0 | gripper_calibrated | bit | 1 calibrated |

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/uart/ -->

# UART commands

Every command the firmware release this site describes understands over the serial port. The kind, the argument
type, the mode a command enters and what it prints are read from the firmware; the descriptions are written by
hand. [Over UART](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/06-operation/uart/) explains the protocol.

## Syntax

```
#<Name> [number]
```

- A **Set/Get** command sets the value when a number follows and prints the current value either way.
- A **Get** command only prints.
- An **Action** command does something; a number after it is ignored. (In firmware 108 and older `#Idle` and
  `#PWM` with a number were answered `Unknown command`.)
- Names are case-sensitive, at most 19 characters; the argument is one word of at most 19 characters, without
  spaces, so a list is written with commas (`#WdFb 2000,0,1000,2`, `#Par 56,0`); the line ends with LF (CR before
  it is fine). Firmware 108 and older allowed 20 characters for name and number together. 256000 baud, 8N1, 3.3 V.
- A name the firmware does not know is answered `Unknown command`.

## Every command

| Command | Kind | Argument | Group |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`#Activate`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |

## By group

- [Motion](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/uart/motion/): setpoints and modes
- [Gains and limits](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/uart/gains/): the loop gains, the limits, the integrator reset, the current loop bandwidth
- [Calibration and motor parameters](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/uart/calibration/): `Cal` and `Calonly`, the motor's R, L and pole pairs, the constants calibration finds, the calibration settings, the encoder table (`Encal`) and the anti-cogging (`Cogcal`)
- [Status and utility](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/uart/utility/): save, reset, defaults, identity, errors, temperature, the cyclic output, any parameter (`Par`), the tool id, the watchdog fallback, the product lock
- [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/uart/gripper/): gripper mode

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/uart/motion/ -->

# Motion

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Iq` | Set/Get | float: current setpoint in mA | Current (torque) control with the given Iq setpoint. Enters **current** mode. | the measured Iq in mA |
| `#Id` | Set/Get | float: current setpoint in mA | Sets the Id setpoint; normally left at 0. Also parameter 58. | the measured Id in mA |
| `#V` | Set/Get | int: speed setpoint in encoder ticks/s | Velocity control with the given speed. Enters **velocity** mode. | the measured speed in ticks/s |
| `#Uq` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | Voltage-torque mode with the given q-axis voltage (no current loop). Enters **voltage torque** mode. | the Uq setpoint in mV |
| `#Ud` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | The d-axis voltage used in voltage-torque mode; does not change the mode. | the Ud setpoint in mV |
| `#Brake` | Action |  | Goes to idle with the motor braking (phases shorted); also the idle behaviour from then on. Not kept by Save: the driver brakes at every power-up. Enters **idle** mode. | `Brake 1` |
| `#HALL` | Action |  | Homing against the sensor on ADDITIONAL2 at 3000 ticks/s, triggered when the pin is low. It holds while the pin stays low and spins on when the pin goes high again (see Send_data_pack_HALL for the CAN form with a chosen speed and trigger). Enters **HALL** mode. | `HALL` |
| `#Coast` | Action |  | Goes to idle with the motor coasting (phases open); also the idle behaviour until the next power-up, which brakes again. Not kept by Save. Enters **idle** mode. | `Coast 0` |
| `#P` | Set/Get | int: position setpoint in encoder ticks | Position control to the given position. Enters **position** mode. | the measured position in ticks |
| `#PD` | Set/Get | int: position setpoint in encoder ticks | Impedance (PD) control around the given position with the gains KP and KD. Enters **PD** mode. | the measured position in ticks |
| `#PDV` | Set/Get | int: speed setpoint in encoder ticks/s | The speed setpoint of the PD loop. | the PD speed setpoint |
| `#PDI` | Set/Get | int: current feedforward in mA | The current feedforward of the PD loop. | the PD current feedforward |
| `#Idle` | Get |  | Goes to idle; the motor coasts or brakes as set by Brake / Coast. | `Idle` |
| `#Close` | Action |  | Leaves open loop and goes back to closed-loop idle. Enters **idle** mode. | nothing |
| `#microstep` | Set/Get | int: microsteps per electrical cycle | The microsteps gosteps makes per electrical cycle (four full steps), 16 by default. | the microstep setting |
| `#stepinterval` | Set/Get | int: step time in µs | The time between two microsteps of gosteps, 1000 µs by default. It is rounded down to whole control cycles of 160 µs, and is 160 µs at the least. | the step interval |
| `#gosteps` | Set/Get | int: number of microsteps (sign = direction) | Moves the given number of microsteps open loop, one every stepinterval, at the voltage set by Openv, then goes to idle. With microstep 16, 16 steps are one electrical cycle: four full steps, 7.2° on a 1.8° motor. Enters **open-loop steps** mode. | `Moving for N steps` |
| `#Openloop` | Set/Get | float: electrical speed in rad/s | Spins the motor open loop, as a plain stepper, with the voltage set by Openv. The voltage is not current-controlled and Ilim does not apply: see Open-loop stepping on Control modes. Enters **open loop** mode. | the open-loop speed |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/uart/gains/ -->

# Gains and limits

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Vlimit` | Set/Get | int: speed in encoder ticks/s | The speed limit: it clamps the speed setpoint of the velocity loop, and in position mode the speed the position loop asks for. The velocity integrator is clamped to the current limit (Ilim), not to this. From firmware 109 a negative number counts as its magnitude. | the current limit |
| `#Vlim` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | The voltage limit of the current loops (Ud and Uq), 6000 mV by default. It keeps the loops of low-resistance steppers stable, and it also caps the top speed. 0, or a value above the supply voltage, means the supply voltage. | the current limit in mV |
| `#Kpp` | Set/Get | float: gain | Kp of the position loop. | the current value |
| `#KP` | Set/Get | float: gain | KP of the impedance (PD) loop. | the current value |
| `#KD` | Set/Get | float: gain | KD of the impedance (PD) loop. | the current value |
| `#Kpv` | Set/Get | float: gain | Kp of the velocity loop. | the current value |
| `#Kpiq` | Set/Get | float: gain | Kp of the Iq current loop; also sets Kpid. | the current value |
| `#Kpid` | Set/Get | float: gain | Kp of the Id current loop. | the current value |
| `#Kiv` | Set/Get | float: gain | Ki of the velocity loop. | the current value |
| `#Kiiq` | Set/Get | float: gain | Ki of the Iq current loop; also sets Kiid. | the current value |
| `#Kiid` | Set/Get | float: gain | Ki of the Id current loop. | the current value |
| `#Ilim` | Set/Get | int: current in mA | The Iq current limit, 1700 mA after #Default. Set it to the rated phase current of your motor; this command clamps it to 2800 mA and takes the magnitude of a negative number (from firmware 109 Send_Limits over CAN stops at 2800 mA too). Calibration uses 1600 mA for its steps and, from firmware 109, puts it back when it ends. | the current limit |
| `#Cbw` | Set/Get | float: bandwidth in Hz, 10 to 625 | The current loop bandwidth. From firmware 109 setting it computes Kpiq and Kiiq at once from R and L, the way calibration does, and prints them (the same as parameter 49); a value outside 10-625, or with R or L at 0, changes nothing. Not kept by Save: 160 Hz at every power-up, but the gains it set are kept. | the bandwidth, then `Kp_iq = …, Ki_iq = …` |
| `#Rstint` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Whether the integral accumulators are reset on every new setpoint. | the setting |

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/uart/calibration/ -->

# Calibration and motor parameters

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#R` | Set/Get | float: resistance in Ω | The phase resistance of the motor (one coil). STEPFOC does not measure it; enter the datasheet value before Cal. Also parameter 76, in mΩ. | the current value |
| `#L` | Set/Get | float: inductance in H | The phase inductance of the motor (one coil); enter the datasheet value before Cal. Also parameter 77, in µH. | the current value |
| `#Kt` | Set/Get | float: Nm/A | The torque constant, found by calibration. | the current value |
| `#KV` | Set/Get | float: rpm/V | The velocity constant, found by calibration. | the current value |
| `#Flux` | Set/Get | float: Wb | The flux linkage, found by calibration. Works over UART from firmware 109; the parser of 108 and older accepted only the lowercase `#flux`, which had no handler. | the current value |
| `#Calonly` | Action |  | The calibration alone: like Cal, but nothing follows it. Save afterwards with Save. Added in firmware 109. Enters **idle** mode. | the calibration log |
| `#Cal` | Action |  | Runs the calibration routine (see Motor parameters and calibration), over the serial port only. Enter R, L and PP first, and the current limit for the motor: it uses its own 1600 mA for its steps and puts the limit back when it ends (firmware 108 and older left 1600 mA). From firmware 109, when it succeeds, the encoder table and then the anti-cogging with the current-sense trim follow by themselves, and everything is saved (about a minute; keep the shaft free). Enters **idle** mode. | the calibration log |
| `#Calonly` | Action |  | The calibration alone: like Cal, but nothing follows it. Save afterwards with Save. Added in firmware 109. Enters **idle** mode. | the calibration log |
| `#Calangle` | Action |  | Runs only an angle-offset search. It uses an older routine than the one in Cal, which gives up after about two minutes and keeps the offset it reached. Prints `Idle` at once, before the search starts. From firmware 109, when parameter 56 is not 0, the anti-cogging is identified again afterwards (with the current-sense trim) and everything is saved: the anti-cogging depends on the offset. After a timeout nothing follows and nothing is saved. From firmware 109 it is refused while the driver is in error. Enters **angle-offset calibration** mode. | `Idle`, at once; `Calangle: not started, the drive is in error (#Error, #Clear)` when it is refused |
| `#Offset` | Set/Get | float: angle in rad | The angle offset between encoder zero and electrical zero, found by calibration. | the current value |
| `#Iqoffset` | Set/Get | int: current in mA | The current used by the angle-offset search. | the current value |
| `#Magnet` | Get |  | Reads the encoder's magnet status. | `Magnet Good` or `Magnet Bad` |
| `#Dir` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | A stored flag that Info prints as `Phase direction`. The control code does not use it in this release; #Default writes 0. | the current value |
| `#Phase` | Get |  | Prints the phase order found by calibration. | `Phase order is: N` |
| `#Resv` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | The voltage calibration starts the resistance test at (not used by STEPFOC, which does not measure resistance). | the current value |
| `#Calpwr` | Set/Get | float: power in W | The power calibration may dissipate in the resistance and inductance tests (not used by STEPFOC). | the current value |
| `#Openv` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | The voltage of the open-loop modes (Openloop, gosteps), 5000 mV at power-up. Calibration does not use it: its open-loop spin has a fixed 5000 mV. Not kept by Save. | the current value |
| `#Opens` | Set/Get | float: electrical speed in rad/s | The electrical speed of Openloop, the same value Openloop sets. Calibration does not use it. | the current value |
| `#Vp` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | Stored, but not used by this firmware: the phase-order check of calibration uses a fixed 3000 mV. | the current value |
| `#Encal` | Set/Get | nothing, or save, all, stop, on, off, state | The encoder table (see Encoder table and anti-cogging). Alone it measures the table and uses it: the field turns the rotor open loop one shaft turn each way at 2048 ticks/s, about 20 s, with the shaft free. `save` also saves; `all` then identifies the anti-cogging and saves both; `stop` aborts; `on` and `off` switch the correction (on only with a measured table, and neither while a run turns the motor); `state`, or any other word, only prints. The same as parameters 52 and 53. Added in firmware 109. | `Encoder table: <state>`, then the table's error in degrees |
| `#Cogcal` | Set/Get | nothing, or save, trim, stop, state | The anti-cogging identification on the drive (see Encoder table and anti-cogging): one motor turn forward and one back in velocity mode at parameter 44's speed (1500 ticks/s, about 22 s), the shaft free to turn. `save` also saves; `trim` first corrects the current-sense zeros from the result and identifies again (not saved: parameter 43 = 5 trims and saves); `stop` aborts, also the encoder part of a combined run; `state`, or any other word, only prints. States 10 and 11 print their own text; 7 and 8, the encoder part of a combined run, show only in parameter 43. Added in firmware 109. | `Anti-cogging identification: <state>`, the speed and the identified cogging in mA rms, and the harmonics when done |
| `#Calibrated` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The calibrated flag. `#Calibrated 1` clears a calibration error without calibrating; the motor may still be uncalibrated. | the flag |
| `#PP` | Set/Get | int: pole pairs | The motor's pole pairs: 50 for a 1.8° stepper, 75 for 1.2°, 100 for 0.9°, 125 for 0.72°. Calibration accepts only these values. Also parameter 78: 1-200, only while idle; from 109 `#PP` answers `PP: not taken (1-200, and only while idle)` otherwise. | the current value |

# Status and utility

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Vmax` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | The supply voltage above which a Vbus error is raised, 29000 mV after #Default. | `Vmax in mV: N` |
| `#Save` | Action |  | Writes the configuration to the EEPROM, and the CAN ID into the bootloader's board ID. Do it after calibration and after tuning. It also writes the serial number held in RAM (1 after a power-up, unless SERNUM set it) over the stored one. | `Save` |
| `#Reset` | Action |  | Resets the driver. From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again. | nothing |
| `#Tlim` | Set/Get | int: temperature in °C | The temperature at which the temperature error is raised; 75 by default. | `Temp limit N` |
| `#Default` | Action |  | Writes the factory defaults to the EEPROM and loads them: the serial number, hardware version and batch date; the gripper flag, heartbeat, watchdog and thermistor (off); the motor parameters and the calibration (cleared); every gain and limit; from firmware 109 also the tool id (0), the watchdog fallback, the calibration ID (0), the anti-cogging set, the encoder table and its trims (cleared), and parameter 56 (back to 2). From firmware 109 the CAN ID is kept (0 only when no valid one is stored). See Defaults. | `Loaded default config!` |
| `#Temp` | Get |  | Prints the thermistor temperature. | °C, or `Temp Off` while the thermistor is disabled |
| `#Term` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Enables the thermistor measurement and the temperature error (off by default). | the setting |
| `#Mode` | Get |  | Prints the control mode. The voltage-torque mode prints `Gripper mode`; HALL, the angle-offset search, open-loop steps (gosteps), gripper mode and the encoder-table run print nothing. | `Idle mode`, `Position control`, `Speed control`, `Current control`, `PD control`, `Open loop`, `Gripper mode`, `Gripper calib mode` |
| `#Vbus` | Get |  | Prints the supply voltage. | mV |
| `#Error` | Get |  | Prints which errors are active. | `No errors!` or `In error state!` followed by one line per active error |
| `#Clear` | Action |  | Clears the errors and goes to idle. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back; a calibration error is cleared only by calibrating (or `#Calibrated 1`). Enters **idle** mode. | `Clear errors` |
| `#Iabc` | Get |  | Prints the phase currents. | `Ia`, `Ib` in mA |
| `#PWM` | Get |  | Prints the PWM duty values. | the duties |
| `#Help` | Action |  | Prints a short command reference. Added in firmware 106. | the reference |
| `#Info` | Action |  | Prints the hardware version, batch date and firmware version, the control loop's execution time, the CAN ID, the calibration state, the thermistor and the supply voltage, the phase direction, phase order and commutation direction, and the motor parameters (pole pairs, angle offset, R, L, Kt, KV). From firmware 109 also the build, the board ID and the calibration ID, the CAN receive overruns and dropped transmits, the product, the current-sense zeros, the tool id, the watchdog and its fallback, settings block 2, the anti-cogging, and at the end the `In force:` section (see Status and diagnostics). Not the serial number (SERNUM), the gains (Param) or the errors (Error). | the report |
| `#Tool` | Set/Get | int: 0 to 255 | The tool id: what the drive is built into, 0 none, 1 SSG-48, 11-33 MSG (tens = rail 1/2/3 = 100/150/200 mm, units = stepper 1/2/3 = 21.5/40/60 mm), 200-254 your own. The same as parameter 1. Kept by Save. Added in firmware 109. | `Tool ID: N`, or `Invalid tool id (0-255)` |
| `#Tone` | Set/Get | f,mA[,ms], or off | A tone through the motor (see Sound): `#Tone 440,250,1000` plays 440 Hz at a loudness of 250 mA for 1000 ms, on the axis parameter 82 picks. mA left out: 200; ms left out: 500; ms 0: until `#Tone off`. 20 Hz up to below 3125 Hz. It plays only while the driver holds or moves; from idle a calibrated driver first holds the position it is at (`#Idle` releases it). `#Tone` alone or `#Tone off` stops all sound. Added in firmware 109. Enters **position** mode. | `Tone 440 Hz, 250 mA, 1000 ms`; from idle first `Holding the position while it plays (#Idle releases it)`; `Tone: not played (…)` when it cannot; `Tone off` |
| `#Par` | Set/Get | int: n, or n,value | Any parameter by its number (see Parameters and buffers): alone it lists every parameter, `#Par 56` reads one, `#Par 56,0` sets it (no spaces); a gain or limit (8-16, 20) takes a decimal, e.g. `#Par 9,0.02` sets Kpv. Added in firmware 109. | `P<n> = <value>`; `refused: out of range, read only, not now, or unknown` when the driver did not take it; `P<n> unknown` |
| `#Product` | Action | nothing, or claim, clear | The product lock: prints this firmware and the board's stamp. `claim` stamps the board as this product (a repaired board, a motor the stamp rule misjudges), `clear` removes the stamp; power-cycle after either. Over UART only. Added in firmware 109. | `Firmware: STEPFOC; board stamp: …` |
| `#WdFb` | Set/Get | int list: time_ms,current_mA,speed_ticks_s,after_action | The watchdog fallback, four numbers at once without spaces, e.g. `#WdFb 2000,0,1000,2`: how long hold or descend runs, descend's current and speed cap, and what follows (0 legacy, 2 brake, 3 coast). The same as parameters 2 to 5, clamped the same way; fewer than four numbers change nothing. Kept by Save. Added in firmware 109. | `Watchdog fallback: … ms, … mA, … ticks/s, then …` |
| `#Param` | Get |  | Prints every gain of every loop. | the gains |
| `#Cyc` | Set/Get | int: interval in ms (0 = off) | Sends position, speed and Iq on its own every interval: `$ <position> <speed> <Iq>`; for BetterSerialPlotter. | `Cyclic disabled` when turned off |
| `#Cyca` | Set/Get | int: interval in ms (0 = off) | Like Cyc, in the Arduino plotter format `Position:x,Speed:y,Iq:z`. | `Cyclic disabled` when turned off |
| `#CANID` | Set/Get | int: 0 to 13 | The CAN node ID. Use 0 to 13: the firmware accepts 14 and 15, but the bootloader reserves them and a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN. Kept over a power cycle after Save, which also writes it into the bootloader's board ID; from firmware 109 Default and a settings reset keep it too. | the ID, or `Invalid CAN ID` |
| `#SERNUM` | Set/Get | int: number | The serial number. This firmware does not read it back from the EEPROM at power-up: it reports 1 until set, and Save writes the value in RAM over the stored one. | `Serial number is: N` |
| `#Activate` | Action |  | Sets the activated flag. | `Controller activated` |
| `#Pullconfig` | Get |  | Prints the whole configuration on one line, for Motor GUI. | the configuration |
| `#LED` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Turns the status LED on or off. | the LED state |

# Gripper

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Gripper` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Whether this driver is a gripper. Save it; `#Default` clears it. | the flag |
| `#Gripcal` | Action |  | Starts the gripper calibration: the jaws find their end stops at 500 mA. It prints nothing when it ends; after about 24 s without both end stops it gives up, uncalibrated. Gripinfo shows the result. Enters **gripper calibration** mode. | `Gripper calibration!` |
| `#Gripinfo` | Get |  | Prints the gripper state: calibrated, activated, end stops, position, current. | the report |
| `#Gripstop` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The gripper E-stop bit. While it is 1 the driver raises the gripper E-stop error on every control cycle: set it to 0, then Clear. | the bit |
| `#Gripact` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The activate bit. | the bit |
| `#Gripcur` | Set/Get | int: current in mA | The current limit of gripper moves, 400 mA at power-up. From firmware 109 a move uses its magnitude, at most the driver's 2800 mA (108 and older used it as sent); see the gripper manual for the safe range. | the setpoint |

| `#Grippos` | Set/Get | int: 0 (open) to 255 (closed) | The position setpoint; also activates the gripper, sets the action bit and goes to gripper mode. Enters **gripper** mode. | the current position |

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/defaults/ -->

# Defaults

The settings of the firmware at the release this site describes: their start values in `common.h`, and what
`EEPROM.cpp` does with each.

- **Start value**: the value in `common.h`. A setting the EEPROM does not keep starts from it at every power-up. A
  kept setting is replaced at power-up by the value in the EEPROM, so its start value is only seen before that.
- **After `#Default`**: what `#Default` writes to the EEPROM and loads; — means `#Default` does not change it.
- **Kept by `#Save`**: whether `#Save` (Send_Save_config) stores it, so that it survives a power cycle.

Internal state (error flags, counters, calibration steps, scratch variables) is left out; the error flags are in
[Errors and LED states](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/errors/). A name after a value, such as `160 (CURRENT_BANDWIDTH_DEFAULT)`, is the
constant in `constants.h` the value comes from. `existing_id` for the CAN ID means that `#Default` keeps a valid
stored ID (0 when none is stored). The settings of firmware 109 that are parameters, the anti-cogging and the
encoder table among them, are in the [parameter table](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/parameters/#every-parameter) with their defaults.

| Variable | Start value | After `#Default` | Kept by `#Save` | Firmware comment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SERIAL_NUMBER` | 1 | 111 in the EEPROM, not read back | written, not read back |  |
| `HARDWARE_VERSION` | 1 | 1 | yes | Version of the Spectral BLDC driver PCB |
| `BATCH_DATE` | 1 | 125 | yes | Date the batch was produced |
| `SOFTWARE_VERSION` | 1 | 109 | no: set by the firmware | Software release |
| `I_AM_GRIPPER` | 1 | 0 | yes | Is motor controller gripper (1) or not (0) |
| `LED_ON_OFF` | 1 | 1 | yes | Use LED for status indication |
| `theta_offset` | 0.0f | 0 | yes | will be determined at calibration |
| `pole_pairs` | 50 | 0 | yes | Number of pole pairs of your Stepper motor |
| `current_control_bandwidth` | 160 (CURRENT_BANDWIDTH_DEFAULT) | — | no | Hz: the current PI gains come from R, L |
| `DIR_` | 1 | 0 | yes | When looking at the magnetic encoder counter-clockwise is POSITIVE rotation. |
| `Phase_order` | 2 | 0 | yes |  |
| `commutation_dir` | 1 | 1 | yes | +1 or -1, auto-detected at calibration so +Iq/+velocity/+rotation map to +encoder rotation |
| `Thermistor_on_off` | 0 | 0 | yes | Are we taking termistor mesurements? 0 is off, 1 is on |
| `Resistance` | 0 | 0 | yes | Resistance of SINGLE PHASE of your BLDC motor |
| `Total_Resistance` | 0 | 0 | yes | = 2 * Resistance + 2 * R_sense + 2 *Rdson |
| `Inductance` | 0 | 0 | yes | Inductance of SINGLE PHASE of your BLDC motor |
| `Kt` | 0 | 0 | yes | Torque constant of your BLDC motor |
| `flux_linkage` | 0 | 0 | yes | Flux linkage of your BLDC motor |
| `KV` | 0 | 0 | yes |  |
| `Max_temperature` | 75 | 75 | yes | Max temperature in degrees |
| `Min_temperature` | -20 | — | no | Min temperature in degrees |
| `Max_Vbus` | 29500 | 29000 | yes | Max vbus voltage in mV |
| `Min_Vbus` | 9000 | — | no | Min vbus voltage in mV |
| `watchdog_time_ms` | 0 | 0 | yes |  |
| `watchdog_action` | 0 | 0 | yes | 0 legacy, 1 hold, 2 brake, 3 coast, 4 descend (watchdog_action.h) |
| `wd_fallback_time_ms` | 2000 | 2000 | yes | how long hold/descend may run before the after-action |
| `wd_fallback_current` | 0 | 0 | yes | mA, descend: the current applied (signed) |
| `wd_fallback_speed` | 1000 | 1000 | yes | ticks/s, descend: the speed cap in either direction |

| `calibration_id` | 0 | 0 in the EEPROM, not read back | written, not read back | parameter 87: new at every successful calibration |
| `tool_id` | 0 | 0 | yes | what the drive is built into: 0 none, 1 SSG-48, 11-33 MSG, 200-254 custom |

| `sense1_offset` | 0 | — | no | current-sense zero of channel 1, ADC counts from 2048 (start-up) |

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/errors/ -->

# Errors and LED states

## The LED

| Pattern | State |
|---|---|
| three short flashes, a pause | normal operation: calibrated, no error |
| fast flashing, about ten times a second | calibration running |
| a few flashes, then blinking for about 2 s after power-up | the bootloader waits for a host before it starts the firmware; it keeps blinking when there is no valid firmware |
| on, steady | error mode, or not calibrated |
| off | no power, or `#LED 0` |

| Normal operation | Calibration | Error mode |
|---|---|---|
| ![Three short flashes and a pause](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/assets/Normal.webp){ width="180" } | ![Fast flashing during calibration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/assets/Calib.webp){ width="180" } | ![On, steady](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/assets/Error2.webp){ width="180" } |

## The error flags

The flags as the firmware keeps them, the line `#Error` prints for each, and where each sits in the two bytes of
Send_Respond_State_of_Errors (bits numbered from the most significant).

| Flag | `#Error` prints | Byte, bit | Raised when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Error` | `In error state!` | 0, 7 | any of the flags below is set (also the error bit of every CAN identifier) |
| `temperature_error` | `Temp error` | 0, 6 | the thermistor reads above `#Tlim` or below −20 °C (with `#Term 1`) |
| `encoder_error` | `Encoder error` | 0, 5 | the encoder reports no magnet (too weak a field) |
| `Vbus_error` | `Vbus error` | 0, 4 | the supply is below 9 V or above `#Vmax` (29000 mV after `#Default`); from firmware 109 a low supply is not checked in the first 500 ms after power-up |
| `Driver_error` | `Driver error (undervoltage, thermal shutdown, or overcurrent)` | 0, 3 | never in this firmware; reserved (STEPFOC reads no fault output of its driver stage) |
| `Velocity_error` | `Velocity error` | 0, 2 | the speed exceeds 30,000,000 ticks/s, a fixed threshold (`Velocity_limit_error`), not `#Vlimit` |
| `Current_error` | `Current error` | 0, 1 | never in this firmware; reserved |
| `ESTOP_error` | `Received ESTOP command` | 0, 0 | Send_ESTOP was received |
| `Calibrated` (0) | `Not calibrated` | 1, 7 (1 = calibrated) | the motor has not been calibrated |
| `Activated` | — | 1, 6 | the activated flag, not an error |
| `Watchdog_error` | `Watchdog error` | 1, 5 | the watchdog time passed without a motion frame or an answered request |
| `wrong_product` | `Wrong firmware for this board (product lock)` | 1, 4 | from firmware 109: the firmware found the other product's stamp, or a calibration its product cannot make, at start-up; it drives nothing |

Gripper mode has its own flags in Respond_Gripper_data_pack: a temperature error (a copy of the thermistor error),
a timeout error (a copy of the CAN watchdog error, not a move timeout) and an E-stop error, which stays while the
E-stop bit is 1; see the [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/gripper/) reference.

## Clearing

`#Clear` and Send_Clear_Error clear every flag except `Calibrated` and go to idle; a flag whose cause persists is
set again at once. The watchdog, E-stop and velocity errors clear and stay clear; the Vbus, encoder and
temperature errors come back until the cause is gone, and so does a gripper E-stop while its E-stop bit is 1.
Calibration clears the calibration error. A wrong product stays until the right firmware is flashed. Clearing a
watchdog error also ends a watchdog hold or descend.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/python/ -->

# Python library

The `Spectral-BLDC` package ([Spectral-BLDC-Python](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python),
`pip install Spectral-BLDC`) has one method per CAN message in `Spectral_BLDC.SpectralCAN`, and
`Spectral_BLDC.CanCommunication` for the bus. [With Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/06-operation/python/) shows how they are used.

## Calls and messages

| Library call | Sends | Answered with | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Send_data_pack_1()` | Send_data_pack_1 (ID 2) | Respond_data_pack_1 | [Motion](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/motion/#send_data_pack_1) |

| `Send_Clear_Error()` | Send_Clear_Error (ID 1) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/system/#send_clear_error) |
| `Send_Watchdog()` | Send_Watchdog (ID 15) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/system/#send_watchdog) |
| `Send_Heartbeat_Setup()` | Send_Heartbeat_Setup (ID 30) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/system/#send_heartbeat_setup) |
| `Send_Parameter()` | Send_Parameter (ID 36) | — | [Parameters and buffers](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/parameters/#send_parameter) |
| `Send_Get_Parameter()` | Send_Get_Parameter (ID 37) | Respond_Parameter | [Parameters and buffers](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/parameters/#send_get_parameter) |
| `Send_Buffer_Read()` | Send_Buffer_Read (ID 41) | — | [Parameters and buffers](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/parameters/#send_buffer_read) |
| `Send_Cogging_Harmonic(), Send_Cogging_Table()` | Send_Buffer_Write (ID 43) | — | [Parameters and buffers](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/parameters/#send_buffer_write) |
| `Send_Sound()` | Send_Sound (ID 44) | — | [Sound](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/sound/#send_sound) |
| `Send_Samples()` | Send_Sound_Samples (ID 45) | — | [Sound](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/sound/#send_sound_samples) |
| `Send_gripper_data_pack()` | Send_gripper_data_pack (ID 61) | Respond_Gripper_data_pack | [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_data_pack) |
| `Send_gripper_calibrate()` | Send_gripper_calibrate (ID 62) | — | [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_calibrate) |

The calls for the messages added in firmware 109 (Send_Parameter, Send_Get_Parameter, Send_Respond_Identity,
Send_Respond_Telemetry, Send_Buffer_Read, Send_Cogging_Harmonic, Send_Cogging_Table, Send_Sound, Send_Samples), and the actions 'Coast' and
'Descend' of Send_Watchdog, come with library 1.21. It also adds calls built on the
parameters, among them Send_Watchdog_Fallback, Send_Tool_ID, Send_Cogging_Mode, Send_Capture_Setup,
Send_Capture_Trigger, Send_Histogram, Send_Cogging_Calibrate and Send_Encoder_Calibrate; the sound calls Send_Tone,
Send_Sound_Stop, Send_Sound_Event, Send_Sound_Play, Send_Sound_Clear, Send_Samples_Play and Send_Samples_Stop on top
of Send_Sound and Send_Samples; and the module `Spectral_BLDC.music` (note names, ringtone melodies, MIDI and WAV
files as queue events and samples, see [Sound](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/109/06-operation/sound/)).

The same release adds `Spectral_BLDC.helpers`, blocking functions that send a request and wait for the answer:
`get_parameter` and `set_parameter` (which reads the value back), `read_identity`, `read_telemetry`, `features`,
`read_buffer`, `capture`, `wait_for_state` (for the encoder table, the anti-cogging and other runs), and
`play_events` and `stream_samples` for sound. They are for setting up and diagnostics, not for the inside of a fast
control loop. The library's `examples` folder shows them at work: `parameters_and_status.py`, `capture.py`,
`calibration_features.py`, `watchdog.py` and `sound.py`.

The same release is stricter about what it sends and reads:

- `Send_Parameter` takes the value itself. Parameters 8 to 16 and 20 are sent as floats
  (`Send_Parameter(16, 1500)` is 1500 mA); every other parameter takes a whole number, and anything else raises
  `ValueError`.
- A position or a speed that does not fit 24 bits, or a current that does not fit 16 bits, raises `ValueError`;
  1.20 wrapped it round. `Send_Voltage_Limit` raises `ValueError` outside 0 to 60000 mV.
- A node ID must be 0 to 15.
- `UnpackData` ignores frames from other nodes, remote frames and extended frames.
- Parameters 79, 80 and 84 to 87 read as unsigned numbers.
- A send that fails returns `False` and is logged once.

## Receiving

`CanCommunication.receive_can_messages(timeout)` returns `(message, ids)`: the raw `python-can` message and a tuple
`ids` with `node_id`, `command_id` and `error_bit` from the identifier, or `(None, None)` after the timeout.
`SpectralCAN.UnpackData(message, ids)` decodes the message into the object's attributes:

| Message | Attributes |
|---|---|
| Respond_data_pack_1 | `position`, `speed`, `current` |
| Respond_data_hall | `position`, `HALL_trigger`, `additional_pin2`, `hall_index` |
| Send_Respond_Encoder_data | `position`, `speed` |
| Send_Respond_Iq_data | `current` |
| Send_Respond_Temperature | `temperature` |
| Send_Respond_Voltage | `voltage` |
| Send_Respond_Device_Info | `HARDWARE_VERSION`, `BATCH_DATE`, `SOFTWARE_VERSION`, `SERIAL_NUMBER` |
| Send_Respond_State_of_Errors | `error`, `temperature_error`, `encoder_error`, `vbus_error`, `driver_error`, `velocity_error`, `current_error`, `estop_error`, `calibrated`, `activated`, `watchdog_error`; from 1.21 also `wrong_product` |
| Send_Respond_Identity (1.21 and newer) | `product_id`, `product_name`, `tool_id`, `firmware_version`, `identity_hardware_version`, `pole_pairs`, `identity_calibrated`, `identity_flags` |
| Send_Respond_Telemetry (1.21 and newer) | `temperature`, `voltage`, the error flags as above, `current` |
| Respond_Parameter (1.21 and newer) | `parameters[number]` (floats for 8-16 and 20), `unknown_parameter`; `tool_id` and `watchdog_fallback` when those parameters come in |
| Respond_Buffer_Data (1.21 and newer) | `capture[index]`, `histogram[bin]`, `cogging_harmonics[slot]`, `cogging_table[index]`, `encoder_table[index]` |
| Send_Respond_Kt | `Kt` |
| Send_Respond_Ping | `ping` (1) |
| Respond_Heartbeat | `heartbeat` (1) |
| Respond_Gripper_data_pack | `gripper_position`, `gripper_current`, `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`, `gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error`, `gripper_calibrated` |

!!! note "Object detection in the library"
    Library 1.20 and older assemble `gripper_object_detection` with the two bits swapped relative to the
    firmware, so they report 1 where the gripper sends 2 (object detected while opening) and 2 where it sends 1
    (object detected while closing); 0 and 3 are unaffected. 1.21 and newer read them right.
